newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Howard sticks to land claim compromise.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Howard sticks to land claim compromise.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Monday he would impose his compromise deal aimed at ending a national row over conflicting claims between Aborigines and farmers, despite opposition from both sides.
"I clearly believe that my model is the better way, the fairer way," he told journalists.
"I will propose at an early date to draft legislation to give effect to that 10-point plan," Howard said after a summit with state and territory leaders aimed at resolving the crisis.
Howard said the legislation would be drafted in consultation with the states and territories and politicians within his Liberal-National coalition, some of whom have criticised the compromise.
Key elements of the 10-point plan include confirming farmers' rights over properties leased from the government, but guaranteed access for Aborigines for traditional purposes.
Miners and farmers have said uncertainty has crippled valuable primary industries since the High Court ruled in December that Aborigines had undefined rights to government land leased to farmers.
Howard said he would also consult Aboriginal groups, angry at the plan's limits on their rights to negotiate over land, over the draft legislation.
But although he was prepared to continue talks with all parties, Howard said he would not accept any changes to the principles of his plan.
"I won't consider amendments that alter the principles of the 10-point plan. People must understand this is not an ambit claim," he said
Howard conceded some states still had reservations about the compromise.

The northern state of Queensland, which has large areas of potentially affected land, has led oppostion to Howard's proposal and demanded complete abolition of Aboriginal rights to land leases to pastoralists.
Howard has said up to 78 percent of Australia's 7.68 million square kms (2.96 million square miles) could be affected by aboriginal land claims.
